content.title:
TIME on Instagram: "Paul Thomas Anderson's 'One Battle After Another' dominated the Oscars, earning Anderson his first three Academy Awards all on the same night: for Best Picture, Best Director, and Best Adapted Screenplay. The film took home six awards overall, following a tight race against 'Sinners,' which entered the Oscars with a record 16 nominations and won a total of four. Anderson's richly imagined political thriller, adapted from Thomas Pynchon's 1990 novel 'Vineland,' showcased acclaimed performances from Leonardo DiCaprio, Teyana Taylor, Chase Infiniti, Benicio del Toro, and Sean Penn, who won the Oscar for Best Supporting Actor for his villainous role in the movie. It was a big night for Anderson, who has been nominated for both Best Director and Best Picture three previous times, for 'There Will Be Blood,' 'Licorice Pizza' and 'Phantom Thread.' "That’s the best part about being on a film crew, is being with people. We need each other," he said while accepting the Best Director award. "This is a wonderful gift, and I’m so happy to call the movies home. This is really terrific. Thank you from the bottom of my heart. I love it.”

See more highlights from the night at the link in bio. 

Photograph by Richard Harbaugh—The Academy/Getty Images"
